newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BATTLE OF THE LITTLE MEN COULD DECIDE FA CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BATTLE OF THE LITTLE MEN COULD DECIDE FA CUP.

text.p: The Italian flair of Gianfranco Zola is pitted against Juninho's Brazilian artistry on Saturday in the English F.A. Cup Final in which Englishmen are likely to be in the minority.

The two diminutive players who have made such a huge impact with their clubs, could hold the key to success as Chelsea attempt to win the Cup for only the second time in their history and Middlesbrough for the first time.

Zola's form for Chelsea since his arrival from Parma in November has been so impressive he has just been named as England's Footballer of the Year. Juninho was voted runner-up and they now both have the chance to shine in English soccer's major showpiece occasion which is being beamed to more than 150 countries worldwide.
But a player with more experience than most of Cup Finals issued a word of warning on the eve of the match.

Chelsea's Mark Hughes, who is bidding to become the first man this century to collect four F.A. Cup winners' medals, said: "Sometimes with all the hype the F.A. Cup Final doesn't live up to expectations.
"But this one has more chance of being open and entertaining. Both sides like to attack and so both sides can be exposed at the back," he added.
Hughes, who scored for Manchester United against Chelsea in the 1994 Cup final, is also likely to play a major role in the outcome.
His successful attacking partnership with Zola has meant Chelsea's first Italian signing, Gianluca Vialli is more often than not left on the bench.

While Vialli may only play for part of the match, if at all, there will be plenty of other overseas stars on show. No Italian has ever played in the cup final -- but there could be as many as five on the pitch plus assorted Norwegians, a Dane, a Romanian, and a Frenchman.

Chelsea boss Ruud Gullit, a Dutchman, becomes the first foreign manager to take a team to the final, but, nationality apart, comparisons with his Middlesbrough counterpart Bryan Robson are inevitable.

Both are player-managers, though neither has played much this season. Both are former national captains, recent world class players, with a wealth of international experience and enviable reputations. Both are young -- Gullit 34 and Robson 40.
But, despite the two sides' similar leadership, makeup and style, they go into the final in very different frames of mind.

Chelsea are riding a tide of optimism. They finished sixth in the league, just missing out on an UEFA Cup place, have overcome stiff opposition such as Liverpool and Wimbledon to reach the Cup final and are enjoying the sort of popularity not seen since their F.A. and Cup Winners' Cup winning heyday of the early 1970s.
"The spirit in the camp is brilliant," said Chelsea's longest-serving player Steve Clarke, a Scot who has been with the club for 10 years.
Middlesbrough could be forgiven for feeling down -- in more ways than one after being relegated from the premier league last week.

Had they not had three points deducted for failing to turn up for a match at Blackburn last December, when Robson said he could not field a team due to illness, injury and suspension, they would have survived.
Middlesbrough are threatening to take the matter to court -- but such a move to get their points back could lead to a possible clash with UEFA and theoretically more punishments.
Meanwhile with a drop into the first division the club are likely to lose their big names. A distressed Juninho said he had to look to his future and that lay perhaps in Spain.
Ravanelli, who despite his 31 goals, has never been at ease in England and has criticised training methods and facilities, is expected to move back to Italy, possibly to AC Milan.
Middlesbrough reached the final of the League Cup this season, only to be beaten in a replay by Leicester.
Their form has been erratic and occasionally it looked like the indefatigable Juninho was trying to make up for the shortcomings of all his team mates.

The F.A. Cup final is all that is left. They have nothing to lose and may glean some comfort from the thought that practically the whole football-watching country, outside southwest London, will be rooting for them.
As Robson remarked: "Relegation has shattered everyone at this club, but at least we have the chance of ending the season on a high."
Probable lineups:
Chelsea: Frode Grodas; Scott Minto, Steve Clarke, Frank Lebouef, Frank Sinclair, Dan Petrescu, Eddie Newton, Roberto di Matteo, Dennis Wise, Mark Hughes, Gianfranco Zola.
Middlesbrough: Ben Roberts; Curtis Fleming, Nigel Pearson, Gianluca Festa, Clayton Blackmore, Fabrizio Ravanelli, Robbie Mustoe, Emerson, Craig Hignett, Juninho, Mikkel Beck.
